Exercise 1: Cookiecutter Setup

Make sure Cookiecutter Data Science is installed: pipx install cookiecutter-data-science

Try running it with: ccds --version

Does this command run and show a version number above 2.something? Great!

Exercise 1.1: Start your DS project

Let's start a new project using Cookiecutter, inspired by CCDS's documentation on their homepage:

  1. Initialise CCDS in directory In the terminal, run ccds
    Discuss what each option does
  2. Initialise git in the repo (if relevant) In the terminal, run git init
  3. Start tracking new files with git git add .

    git commit -m "Initial CCDS commit"

    What does git add . do?
Also: what's in .gitignore?

Exercise 1.2: Push to GitHub

The pipeline you will build in the coming exercises ends up being tested in CI/CD, so the code needs a home on github.com. If you don't want to use your normal github.com user for this course, feel free to create a dummy one.

  1. Create a new repo on github.com Create an empty repository (no README, no .gitignore, no license - you already have all of those).
  2. Push your code to this new remote (hint: these lessons covered it) git remote add origin git@github.com:<username>/<new_repo>.git

    git push

    We are actually missing an argument to git push. Can you find out what?
    Hint: git push --set-upstream origin main
  3. Work on a branch Good developer practice is to not work directly on main since that is reserved for production code. Instead create a new branch for the coming exercises:

    git checkout -b w04-project-setup

    Why is it a good idea to keep main "green" (i.e. always working)?

From here on, work on feature branches and merge them to main via pull requests once the exercises are done - that is the same workflow you will use in any real project.
